correctness.rationale: For d>=3 over C the Hessian forces a maximally tangent point onto a coordinate axis, and each axis point gives contact d by restricting the Fermat equation to its line. The different-pencil crossings are ordinary and distinct: a three-pencil concurrence would require three cyclic coordinate ratios with product 1 but with all d-th powers -1. At the three coordinate centers the blowup separates the distinct tangent directions and contributes one node per pencil line. The connected dual graph therefore has 3d+3 rational components, 3d^2+3d nodes and genus 3d^2-2; each component has valency at least three. In the reduced Laplacian presentation, taking same-pencil differences gives m times each difference, and the primitive sum t_a is the only difference coordinate coupled to the remaining relations. This splits off 3(d-2) independent C_m factors integrally. The first two base-line relations eliminate their hubs with unit coefficients; substituting them in the hub relations leaves d^2(2y_1-y_2-y_3)-t_1-dt_2-dt_3 and its switched counterpart. The third base-line relation eliminates y_3 with coefficient m-2d=1 after passing to differences, leaving the stated 5-by-5 presentation. For p not dividing m the three t_a disappear and the last block has Smith factors d^2 and 3d^2. For p|m and p!=3 that block is invertible, leaving three m-primary factors. For p=3|m, write w=r_1-r_2: the first bottom relation eliminates r_2 with coefficient d^2, and the difference relation is 3[d^2 w+(d-1)(t_1-t_2)/3]=0. The bracket is a valid 3-adic generator since d is a unit and 3|(d-1). This adds a separate C_3 to the three m-primary factors. Reassembling in divisibility order yields both formulas, and the determinant gives the claimed order. The Néron interpretation is the conditional unit-thickness split semistable one, not a claim of existence of a family.
residual_risks: The Smith replay checks graph arithmetic on a finite range, not the geometry or all-degree theory. No assertion is made about arbitrary thicknesses, positive characteristic, or an existing model with this special fiber.

evidence: The multipartite theorem supplies the critical group for K_{d,d,d} and the other stated complete multipartite cases. The resolved graph is not complete multipartite: any two hubs are nonadjacent and have unequal neighbor sets, whereas nonadjacent distinct vertices in a complete multipartite graph are in the same part and have equal neighbor sets.
The geometry sources already give the line arrangement; Moe counts the ordinary double intersections and the three pencil centers before blowup.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Deleting the three hubs recovers the known multipartite graph, but restoring a degree-d hub is not a bridge attachment. The edges change both line degrees and the torsion, and the complete-multipartite theorem does not specialize to this graph. Competing general graph results found did not provide matching integral invariant factors for the unequal blow-up.

evidence: The graph is equivalently the triangle with one pendant at each corner, replacing each corner by d independent twins and leaving each pendant a singleton, with complete bipartite edges replacing base edges. The same invariant is the torsion cokernel of the full Laplacian (or finite reduced-Laplacian cokernel), and conditionally the geometric component group of the corresponding Jacobian.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Collapsing whole pencil classes to an equitable quotient is generally only a rational simplification. Here the p=3 residual relation and the m-torsion difference classes are integral data, so neither an equitable quotient spectrum nor a spanning-tree formula supplies the claimed invariant factors. No matching complete formula was recovered under these equivalent descriptions.
